title: How to change virtual background in Zoom on Mac: step by step for Zoom Workplace
metaTitle: How to Change Virtual Background in Zoom on Mac
description: How to change virtual background in Zoom on Mac, step by step. Settings path, in-meeting steps, your own image, shortcuts and fixes for Zoom Workplace.
targetKeyword: how to change virtual background in zoom on mac
secondaryKeywords: zoom virtual background not working mac
intro: To change your virtual background in Zoom on Mac, open Zoom Workplace, click your profile picture, choose Settings, then go to Video & effects and click Virtual backgrounds. During a meeting, click the arrow next to Video, choose Video & effect settings, and pick a new background from the panel that opens.
tldr: Desktop path: profile picture > Settings > Video & effects > Virtual backgrounds.
In a meeting: click the arrow next to Video, then choose Video & effect settings.
Your own image must be a 24-bit PNG or JPG, up to 15MB.
Zoom lists no Mac keyboard shortcut for virtual backgrounds. ⌘⇧V only starts and stops video.

stats.label: of 610 videoconferencing users in a 2023 Singapore survey used a virtual background of some kind
of all 610 survey respondents used an image as their virtual background

blocks.text: Most people on a Mac use the desktop app, so start there. Open Zoom Workplace, click your profile picture in the top-right corner, choose Settings, click Video & effects, then click Virtual backgrounds. Pick a thumbnail to apply it. The rest of this page covers the in-meeting route, your own photos, the web app, shortcuts, Mac requirements, and the problems that stop a background from changing.
What you need before you start

You need Zoom Workplace, a camera Zoom can use, and a Zoom account you can sign in to. Virtual backgrounds run on your Mac's processor, so the machine has to meet Zoom's rules. Most Macs from the last several years clear the bar. Older machines may open the app and still lack some options. Check the requirements section before you spend time in menus.

items: Zoom Workplace installed and signed in with your meeting account
Camera access turned on for Zoom in System Settings
macOS 10.15 or later for the Zoom Workplace desktop app
Optional: a PNG or JPG of 15MB or less for your own background

blocks.text: Not sure which macOS you run? Choose Apple menu > About This Mac. The macOS version appears in the window. Compare it with the 10.15 minimum for the desktop app.
Which route to use on your Mac

Use Settings when you want a background ready before anyone joins. Use the in-meeting route when you need a quick change mid-call. Use the web app only when you join from Chrome or Edge in a browser. Each route reaches the same set of thumbnails, so the choice comes down to timing.
Change your virtual background from Settings

The Settings route works before a meeting starts, and it is the one most people need. Zoom's current support article uses the tab name Video & effects, with a Virtual backgrounds tab inside it. Zoom's older Virtual Backgrounds article uses Backgrounds & Filters. If your labels do not match, look for the Virtual backgrounds tab and ignore the exact wording of the parent tab.
Inside the Virtual backgrounds tab you see a short row of choices. Each one behaves differently, so pick with purpose.

items: None turns the effect off and shows your real room.
Blur softens everything behind you and keeps you in focus.
Zoom's defaults, plus any recently uploaded images or videos, appear as thumbnails. Click one to use it.
The add icon uploads your own file from your Mac.
Generate, next to Create AI virtual background, makes an AI background.

blocks.text: Generate needs a higher account type. Zoom's admin article says AI-generated backgrounds require Pro, Business, or Enterprise. Managing default backgrounds for a team needs Pro, Business, Education, or Enterprise. If you are on a plan below those, Generate may not show, and that is the reason, not a fault in your Mac.

blocks.title: Naming check
blocks.text: Zoom Workplace was called the Zoom app until April 2024. Older pages say Backgrounds & Filters. If a label differs from this page, look for Virtual backgrounds inside Settings.
Change the Zoom background during a meeting

You can switch backgrounds while you are on a call. Click the arrow next to Video in the meeting controls toolbar, then choose Video & effect settings. A Video & effects panel opens on the side, with the Virtual backgrounds tab selected. Click a new thumbnail, then close the panel.

Zoom Workplace 6.7 changed the in-meeting toolbar. Zoom's blog says some buttons moved under a More menu, and meeting settings moved into one right-hand panel. The arrow next to Video may sit somewhere else on your build. This page has not checked that in the app, so look under More first if the arrow is missing.
Use your own photo or video as a background

The add icon takes your own file. Zoom is strict about format, so check the table before you upload. Crop the image to match your camera's shape, or the edges can cut into your head or shoulders. Zoom suggests an image at least 1280x720 pixels if you are unsure.

blocks.caption: Custom image rules from Zoom's support article KB0060387
rows: At least 1280x720 pixels if you are unsure

blocks.text: Say you have a photo of your bookshelf saved as a JPEG under 15MB. The format and size rules pass. The crop still decides what you see, so test it before a call. Hold your hand near the frame and check whether it stays inside the picture.
The Settings tab also lists recently uploaded videos. Zoom's upload rules in the table name images only. Check the file format before you rely on a video, because the rules above do not cover it.

Plenty of people use custom backgrounds. In a 2023 survey of 610 videoconferencing users in Singapore, 72.6 percent used some kind of virtual background. Image backgrounds came first at 36.6 percent, ahead of blur at 26.6 percent and video at 9.5 percent. That survey covers one country and one year, so read it as a snapshot.
Green screen mode and the color picker

Zoom has a second option for people with a physical green screen. Turn on I have a green screen in the Virtual backgrounds tab if you hang a green sheet or fabric behind you. The color selector works only after you choose an image with that option on.

Zoom's automatic color guess can pick a shade near skin tone. When it does, part of your face can disappear. Pick a color that does not match your shirt, hair, or eyes. If the guess looks wrong, choose the color yourself with the selector.

Lighting matters more than the exact green. Stand where light falls evenly on your face, and keep the sheet flat. Zoom's requirements list macOS 10.9 or higher for video with a green screen. The desktop app itself needs 10.15, so that older floor rarely matters on a current Mac.
Keyboard shortcuts that touch video on Mac

Zoom's keyboard shortcut article lists two shortcuts that matter for video. Command plus Shift plus V starts and stops your video. Command plus Shift plus N switches to another camera. Neither one opens the Virtual backgrounds tab or changes the background.

blocks.title: No background shortcut
blocks.text: Zoom's hot keys article lists no Mac shortcut for virtual backgrounds. Shortcuts can change between builds, so check the keyboard shortcuts section in Settings if one fails.
A practical order helps. Turn your video off, change the background in Settings, then press ⌘⇧V to start your video. That keeps a half-set background off the call.
Change the background in the Zoom web app

If you join from a browser, the steps differ. The web app uses the meeting toolbar, not the desktop Settings window. Zoom lists Chrome and Edge for the web app, along with Chrome OS. Safari and Firefox do not appear on that list, so use Chrome or Edge if the option is missing.

items: Join the meeting in Chrome or Edge.
In the meeting controls, click the up arrow next to Start Video or Stop Video.
Click Choose Background.
Pick an image, or click the add icon to upload your own.
Close the window to return to the meeting.

blocks.text: The web app also needs a processor with at least 4 logical cores. Four real cores, or two cores with four threads, meet the rule. If the option is still missing, check the processor line in the requirements table before you try other fixes.
Check your Mac requirements before you troubleshoot
Zoom's requirements split by app, by image or video, by green screen use, and by processor. Each one sets its own floor. The table gathers the Mac rules from Zoom's pages.

blocks.caption: Mac requirements from Zoom's system requirements pages
rows: macOS 10.13 or higher, with Apple M-Series or Intel Core i3, i5, i7, i9, or Xeon with 4 cores or higher
6 or more Intel cores or Apple M-Series, plus the HD guidelines and the app's minimum version
Chrome OS, or Chrome or Edge, with at least 4 logical cores

blocks.text: Two details trip people up. Intel Core i3 needs 8th generation or newer. Without a green screen, outgoing video is capped at 720p. Reaching 1080p needs the processor rule, the HD guidelines, and the app's minimum version.

Older Macs face a harder limit. Zoom says version 6.7.7 is the last Zoom Workplace release for macOS below 10.15. If your Mac runs an older system, plan an OS upgrade, or join from Chrome or Edge on the web.

Virtual environments are a special case. Zoom says virtual background without a green screen is not supported when the desktop app runs inside a virtual environment. Some VDI setups and thin clients may not support it either. If you use a company virtual desktop, ask IT before you chase a fix.
Zoom virtual background not working on Mac: fixes

Most failures come down to three things. An admin has locked the feature, Zoom cannot use the camera, or the background package did not download. Check the admin lock first, since you cannot fix that from your Mac.

A grayed-out Virtual backgrounds toggle means an admin has locked it. Admins change this in the Admin Center under Settings > Meeting > In Meeting (Advanced) > Virtual background. They can set it at account or group level. You cannot override that lock from the desktop app.

Next, check camera permission. Choose Apple menu > System Settings, click Privacy & Security, then click Camera. Turn on Zoom in the list. Apple lists only apps that have asked for camera access, so start a test call first if Zoom is missing.

Then check the background package. Zoom's older article says that when you select a background, Zoom may ask you to download a package for virtual background without a green screen. Accept it, then try again. That article is written for the Virtual Backgrounds app and asks for desktop client 5.7.3 or higher, so treat it as a lead for the built-in feature.

If the tab disappears after you enable the setting, sign out, sign back in, and check again. If your video has black bars on the sides, turn on HD video in Video settings. Zoom's support article gives both fixes.
Common mistakes people make with Zoom backgrounds

items: Skipping the 1280x720 suggestion when you are unsure about size. Zoom offers that size as a safe starting point.
Uploading a file over 15MB, or a format Zoom does not accept. Save it as a 24-bit PNG or JPEG first.
Turning on green screen mode with no green screen. The color guess can cover your face.
Hunting for a Mac shortcut for backgrounds. Zoom's list has none.
Following an old guide that says Backgrounds & Filters and getting lost. Look for Virtual backgrounds instead.
Missing the More menu after the 6.7 toolbar cleanup, then deciding the feature is gone.
Leaving the crop to chance. Preview the image in the tab before you go live.

blocks.text: Zoom Workplace names and version changes

The app has changed names and layouts in the last few years. Zoom renamed the desktop client Zoom Workplace in April 2024, and before that it was called the Zoom app. Zoom Workplace 6.7, updated December 15, 2025, moved some toolbar items under More. Zoom Workplace 7.0.0 began rolling out progressively from March 23, 2026.
Zoom's post on version 7.0.0 says it added an AI tab. It does not describe changes to Video & effects or background controls. Your Settings layout may therefore match this page even on a newer build.

blocks.title: A note on versions
blocks.text: Zoom's support pages give no exact minimum build for virtual backgrounds on a Mac. Third-party sites list version numbers that disagree with each other. Use your macOS version and Zoom's requirement tables instead.
Test your background before a real meeting

Run a short test call before a real meeting. Turn your camera on and look at how you appear. Check the edges around your hair and shoulders, and check the light on your face. Then adjust the room before you change the background again. Most edge problems come from light and clutter, not from the setting itself.

Keep two or three backgrounds you like, so you can switch fast. Keep one plain option, such as None or Blur, for days when the room already looks fine on its own. Zoom keeps recently uploaded images in the same tab, so the next switch takes one click.

faq.question: Where is the virtual background setting in Zoom on Mac?
faq.answer: Open Zoom Workplace, click your profile picture in the top-right corner, choose Settings, click Video & effects, then click Virtual backgrounds. During a meeting, click the arrow next to Video and choose Video & effect settings.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to change the virtual background on Mac?
faq.answer: No. Zoom's keyboard shortcut article lists Command plus Shift plus V to start and stop video, and Command plus Shift plus N to switch cameras. It lists no shortcut for virtual backgrounds.

faq.question: What image size should I use for a custom Zoom background?
faq.answer: Zoom accepts a 24-bit PNG or a JPG or JPEG file up to 15MB. Crop it to your camera's aspect ratio. If you are unsure, use an image at least 1280x720 pixels.

faq.question: Why is the Virtual backgrounds tab missing?
faq.answer: Sign out of Zoom Workplace, sign back in, and check Settings again. If the toggle is grayed out, an admin has locked the setting in the Admin Center, and only an admin can change it.

faq.question: Can I change my virtual background in the Zoom web app on Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, in Chrome or Edge. Click the up arrow next to Start Video or Stop Video, click Choose Background, then pick an image or upload one. Zoom does not list Safari or Firefox for the web app.

faq.question: Do I need a green screen to use virtual backgrounds on Mac?
faq.answer: No. Green screen mode is optional. Without one, Zoom supports image backgrounds on macOS 10.13 or higher with an Apple M-Series or a suitable Intel processor.

faq.question: What does Error 10012 mean when I pick a background?
faq.answer: Zoom's older Virtual Backgrounds article says Error 10012 means the background package is missing. Select a background and download the package when Zoom asks. No official page for the built-in feature confirms this fix.

faq.question: Can an admin stop me from changing my virtual background?
faq.answer: Yes. Admins can enable or disable virtual backgrounds at account or group level. A grayed-out toggle means an admin has locked it, and only an admin can change it.

task: Change your virtual background in Zoom on Mac
appliesTo: Zoom Workplace desktop app on macOS, and the Zoom web app in Chrome or Edge
requirements: Zoom Workplace installed and signed in on your Mac
macOS 10.15 or later for the Zoom Workplace desktop app
A camera Zoom can use, with camera access turned on in System Settings
Optional: a custom image in 24-bit PNG or JPG format, up to 15MB
For the web app: Chrome or Edge, with a processor that has at least 4 logical cores

steps.name: Open Zoom Workplace and sign in
steps.text: Open Zoom Workplace from your Dock or Applications folder. Sign in with the account you use for meetings. Settings changes apply to that account.
steps.tip: If Zoom offers an update, install it first so your menus match this guide.

steps.name: Open Settings from your profile picture
steps.text: Click your profile picture in the top-right corner of the Zoom window. Click Settings in the menu that opens.

steps.name: Open the Video & effects tab
steps.text: In the Settings window, click the Video & effects tab. This tab holds the camera and background options.
steps.tip: Older guides call this tab Backgrounds & Filters.

steps.name: Open the Virtual backgrounds tab
steps.text: Click the Virtual backgrounds tab. You see None, Blur, Zoom's defaults, your recently uploaded images and videos, and the add icon.

steps.name: Choose a background
steps.text: Click a thumbnail to apply it. Click None to turn the effect off. Blur softens the room behind you while you stay in focus.

steps.name: Add your own image (optional)
steps.text: Crop the file to match your camera's shape before you upload it. Click the add icon, choose a 24-bit PNG or JPG under 15MB, then click it to apply.
steps.tip: If you are unsure about size, use an image at least 1280x720 pixels.

steps.name: Change it during a meeting
steps.text: In a meeting, click the arrow next to Video in the meeting controls toolbar. Choose Video & effect settings, then pick a new thumbnail in the side panel.
steps.tip: After a 6.7 toolbar cleanup, some buttons sit under More. Check there if the arrow is missing.

steps.name: Check the result before your meeting
steps.text: Turn your video on and check how you appear. Look at the edges around your hair and shoulders, and check the light on your face.
steps.tip: Zoom's list has no shortcut for the background itself, only for starting or stopping video.

troubleshooting.fix: Sign out of Zoom Workplace, sign back in, then check Settings > Video & effects again. If it is still missing, ask your admin whether the feature is turned off for your account.

troubleshooting.problem: Virtual backgrounds toggle is grayed out
troubleshooting.fix: An admin has locked it. Admins change it in the Admin Center under Settings > Meeting > In Meeting (Advanced) > Virtual background.

troubleshooting.problem: Zoom cannot use the camera for backgrounds
troubleshooting.fix: Choose Apple menu > System Settings, click Privacy & Security, then click Camera. Turn on Zoom in the list. If Zoom is not listed, start a test call first.

troubleshooting.problem: Error 10012 when you pick a background
troubleshooting.fix: Zoom's older Virtual Backgrounds article says to select a background and download the package when prompted. That article asks for desktop client 5.7.3 or higher. No official page for the built-in feature confirms this fix.

troubleshooting.problem: Black bars on the sides of your video
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on HD video in Video settings, as Zoom's support article suggests.
